defects.statement: NginxBackend restored the previous vhost when its own test or reload failed, but exposed no inverse for a successful apply. A route that installed cleanly yet did not serve traffic could be detected as broken with no way to restore the working vhost.
defects.fix: NginxBackend and CompositeBackend gained ApplyWithCompensation; PublicRoutePlanner gained ApplyWithCompensation that fails loudly when a backend cannot produce an inverse.

defects.statement: DNS-plus-HTTPS route verification existed only inside CloudflareBackend.verifyHTTPS. Any second verification path would have duplicated the resolver and dial logic, which is the class of divergence that produced this outage.
defects.fix: Extracted a single shared resolver/dial-override transport builder into internal/httpclient, consumed by the route prober. It is built on hardenTransport so TLS verification cannot be disabled on any probe path.

defects.statement: The canary could not detect a non-discriminating health path. Against a catch-all application that serves its shell with HTTP 200 for every path, the health-path assertion proves only that something answered, and a wrong health path is indistinguishable from a correct one. Found during live validation on 2026-09-07: a route-only attach for Astillero with health path /__route_canary_expected_failure__ was allowed by the gate. Read-only probes confirmed astillero.sharegap.net returns a byte-identical 2252-byte body for /health, the deliberately bad path, and a random path, so the route genuinely was serving and the gate evaluated it correctly. The defect is the missing negative control, not a gate bypass.
defects.fix: Added an optional negative-control probe (detect_catch_all). Each probe additionally requests a random unpredictable control path and fingerprints both bodies; an indistinguishable pair is classified health_path_not_discriminating. Warning by default because serving a catch-all is legitimate, promotable to a blocking failure via require_discriminating_health_path. An explicit expected_body_contains that holds is real evidence and suppresses the warning.

defects.statement: When the policy derived no targets for a route, the gate returned success indistinguishably from having verified a healthy route. An operator who had just watched a gate fail to block had no way to tell 'checked and healthy' from 'checked nothing'.
defects.fix: The no-target path is now a separate branch that logs a warning naming the route coordinate and hostname, and does not record a canary state that would imply verification occurred.

defects.statement: Migration 000060 pinned the route canary classification set in CHECK constraints on route_canary_state and route_canary_events. The health_path_not_discriminating classification added for D3 was never admitted by those constraints. Build, vet and the full test suite were green because nothing connects a Go constant to a SQL CHECK constraint. On the live candidate built from 67118759 the service started healthy and then every route canary supervisor upsert failed with SQLSTATE 23514, forcing an operator rollback to 66bb4834.
defects.fix: Added versioned migration 000061_route_canary_health_path_classification, which drops the generated 000060 constraints by locating them in pg_constraint rather than assuming a naming convention, and re-adds explicitly named constraints including the new value. 000060 was left untouched because it is already applied in production. The down migration normalizes withdrawn state rows to route_ok and deletes affected lineage rows, since an append-only event must not be restated as something never observed.
defects.prevention: Added internal/db/route_canary_constraint_conformance_test.go, which replays the route canary migrations in order, computes the value set left in force, and asserts it matches domain.AllRouteCanaryClassifications, AllRouteCanaryPerspectives and AllRouteCanaryTransitions in both directions. Verified by removing 000061 and observing the test fail with the SQLSTATE 23514 explanation. domain.Valid now derives from the same enumeration so the list cannot drift from validation either.

defects.statement: The route canary detail endpoint could not be used as documented. RouteCanaryHandler.Get wrote the bare state object with writeJSON instead of the {data: ...} detail envelope (writeData) every other single-resource endpoint uses, so the web client, which unwraps data.data, received undefined. Separately, Get and ListEvents built the route key without a deployment unit unless ?deployment_unit_id= was passed, but every valid plan carries a non-nil DeploymentUnitID (ValidateDesiredPublicRoute), so every stored row is keyed with a unit and every unit-less lookup returned 404, contradicting the documented contract that the unit is needed only when a service has more than one managed route per environment. AC8 was verified by file references only, so no test exercised the real response shape. Found by independent review of the combined route canary tree (integration 22b84636).
defects.fix: Get now writes the detail through writeData. ListEvents keeps the {data, total, limit, offset} list envelope shared with List (data is always an array, never null). When deployment_unit_id is omitted, both endpoints resolve the route from stored state for (service, environment, normalized hostname) via ListStateByEnvironment: exactly one match is used (200, with the resolved deployment_unit_id in the body), no match is 404, and several matches are 409 naming the candidate units and asking for deployment_unit_id. An explicit deployment_unit_id addresses that key directly as before; an invalid one is 400. Query validation (limit) runs before resolution.

defects.statement: Post-deploy gate outcomes were persisted but never announced. RouteCanaryGate.record saved gate verdicts through UpsertStateWithEvent with thresholds 1/1 and held no events.Publisher, while every consumer of route transitions (notifications, alerting, the Nostr projector) learns of them only from RouteCanaryChanged events that RouteCanarySupervisor published for transitions it observed itself. A gate that recovered a supervisor-opened outage therefore sent no route.canary_recovered, and the supervisor, seeing a closed route_ok afterwards, never reported one either; a gate-opened outage sent no route.canary_outage_opened. Found by independent review of the combined route canary tree (integration 22b84636).
defects.fix: The gate takes an events.Publisher, wired in internal/app/app.go to the same bus as the supervisor, and publishes persisted transitions through publishRouteCanaryTransition, the single implementation shared with the supervisor, so event types, payloads and severities are identical. Unpersisted transitions are not announced. Publication uses context.WithoutCancel; the gate's other behavior, including rollback on a non-canceled context, is unchanged.
